title: S2i harness_depth and small-task fast path in shadow: deterministic depth level 0-4 from existing task fields, fast path skips Jev, skill routing, strategy lookup and scouts for level 0-1, promotion feature fast_path (P24, P25, P26)
spec:
Create orchestrator/harness_depth.py. level(task, *, tasks, cfg, history) -> {"level": 0..4, "reasons": [...], "eligible_fast_path": bool}. Deterministic rules in order: 4 when constraints.architectural, any scope path matches [review] security_paths or migrations area globs, complexity >= 8, or the task is a goal container; 3 when complexity 6-7, unresolved depends_on, or constraints.route is spec_review; 2 when complexity 4-5; 1 when complexity <= 3, scope <= 3 files, no security path, no dependency unresolved; 0 additionally when every acceptance line except the gate line is a test id (tests/test_x.py::test_y) and history first-pass rate for the task_class is >= 0.8 over at least 5 samples (history from scorecard rows; missing history means level 1, never 0). Fast path = level 0 or 1: in daemon dispatch and spawn packet building skip jev_route, skill routing (skills=None path), strategy lookup, context-router Jev calls and scout suggestions; keep hooks, tests-green, security review by path and human PR untouched. [harness].depth_mode = "shadow" (dated comment; off|shadow|active): shadow records a decision_log row kind harness_depth (add to KINDS) per dispatch with candidates 0..4, selected, reasons, would_skip list, and changes nothing; active applies the skips and stamps pipeline.harness_level. promotion FEATURES entry fast_path with criteria: at least 20 shadow rows at level 0-1, and once active first-pass rate of fast-path tasks not below the shadow baseline and lower tokens per accepted task; demotion on a fast-path task that needed two fix rounds. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/15-harness-depth.md with the distribution of levels over the real bus tasks of this repository (run level over all merged execute tasks and tabulate).
Spec review T-1070 folded in: (a) The fast-path skip list names only behaviours that exist: jev_route in daemon dispatch, skill routing where it really runs (spawn._prepare_skills in run_worker for the Claude fallback executor, scout, review, challenge and spec_review roles), context-router Jev calls, and spec review; drop 'strategy lookup' and 'scout suggestions' from the list and from would_skip (strategy.py is reporting-only and no scout suggestion exists). The active test verifies jev_route and _prepare_skills are not called for a level 0-1 task and the security review still fires. (b) 'architectural' is not a persisted constraint: level 4 uses constraints.architectural when present (Planner-set) OR the planner_taxonomy classification of the task computed at dispatch (planner_taxonomy.classify), whichever says architectural; document that real tasks today carry it only through the classifier. (c) History: first-pass rate per task_class uses first_pass_defined_count as the sample count (rows where first_pass is known), threshold 5; compute the history table ONCE per daemon tick (cache on the pool or a module-level cache keyed by the runs directory mtime) and reuse it for every candidate task in that tick.
Spec review T-1094 folded in: (a) constraints.route == "spec_review" IS persisted: the Planner sets it when filing every complexity >= 6 task of this goal (look at any queued task JSON under the main checkout's .orchestrator/tasks; a worktree carries none), so the level-3 rule keeps it; drop the 'unresolved depends_on' clause because level() runs only for tasks bus.ready() already admitted (note that in the docs). (b) The migrations glob lives at [review.areas.migrations].paths in pool.toml (nested under areas next to auth, interfaces, data_deletion); read it from there. (c) Self-refusal in active mode mirrors skill routing's existing pattern (the daemon notify line 'active skill routing refused; using shadow'): before applying skips, call promotion.evaluate("fast_path", ...) and, when the criteria are unmet, run as shadow and notify once per tick; add tests/test_harness_depth.py::test_active_refuses_to_shadow_when_promotion_criteria_unmet. (d) Cross-feature sample: a fast-path task still records one skill_selection decision_log row with selected empty and reason fast_path (and the jev_route row with reason fast_path) so the skill_routing and jev_routing promotion samples are not silently skewed; document this interaction in 15-harness-depth.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_harness_depth.py::test_levels_from_rules (security path task 4, complexity 6 task 3, complexity 5 task 2, small localized task 1, small task with test-id acceptance and good history 0)
